method: The waist radius is the waist divided by the arc angle: a full circle wraps 2 pi radians around the waist, a three-quarter circle 1.5 pi, a half circle pi and a quarter circle 0.5 pi, so the same waist needs a larger radius as fullness falls. The inner cut radius subtracts the seam allowance from the waist radius so the seam line sits back from the cut edge. The outer cut radius adds the finished length and the hem allowance. The pattern block is the rectangle one piece fits in: twice the outer radius by twice the outer radius for a full or three-quarter circle, twice by once for a half circle and the outer radius square for a quarter circle. The finished hem length is the arc angle times the waist radius plus the finished length. Waist is limited to 10 to 80 inches (25 to 203 cm), finished length to 2 to 60 inches (5 to 152 cm), seam allowance to 0 to 1 inch (0 to 2.5 cm), hem allowance to 0 to 4 inches (0 to 10 cm) and usable fabric width to 20 to 120 inches (50 to 305 cm); text, exponent notation, empty fields and out of range values are refused with the field named. The page assumes an even hem, a straight waist seam with no waistband, casing or lining, and a single-piece cut; directional prints, nap, bias stretch, pattern matching, squaring the fabric and pieced panels need extra allowance, and a test garment is the check for fit. It stores, uploads and transmits nothing and runs entirely in the browser.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Circle skirt: a circle skirt is cut as a full, three-quarter, half or quarter circle with the waist on the inner arc.
